questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Writing a power in scientific notation
questions.learningObjective: evaluate a power of ten times a coefficient as a plain number
questions.stem: Amateur astronomer Nadia Okonkwo logs a nebula's brightness as 6.2 times 10 to the fifth power photons. What plain number belongs in her chart?
questions.explanation: Multiplying 6.2 by 10 to the fifth power means 6.2 times 100,000, which is 620,000. Adding exponents instead of using the power of ten, or shifting the decimal the wrong way, records a different quantity.
questions.hint: Multiply the coefficient by 10 raised to the exponent.

options.misconception: leaves the coefficient below 1 instead of shifting the decimal

options.text: 3,700,000,000 kilometres written out in full

questions.explanation: Standard form needs a coefficient from 1 up to 10, so 3.7 times 10 to the ninth power qualifies. A coefficient of 0.37 or 37 breaks the rule, and spelling the digits out is not scientific notation.
